about: Where an auto chain ends is decided by the registry's `turn_end.bounds` (its K), not by a host. Each case runs `segments` of turn ends on one observation basis (a segment is a basis label and a count, `K` standing for the registry's number), every one of which continues, then one `final` turn end on a basis, which `then` says continues or ends the chain with `unattended_residual`. `actor` is the run view's `turn_end_actor`. Pi (`turn-end.test.ts`) and Claude (`test_claude_adapter.py`) read this file, so the two hosts answer the same chains. `sequences` give what each turn end hands the agent: `reason` (the core's own reason), `continue` (`unattended_continue`, which asks for action and never offers the stop), `residual-directive` (the last continuation, the one before a bound: `unattended_residual` as the directive, so the model sees the stop) and `end` (the turn that ends the chain, `unattended_residual`). A step runs `turns` turn ends on `basis`; `fresh` is a new basis at every turn end.

cases.name: author: K - 1 turn ends on one basis continue, the K-th ends
author: one turn end short of K, the next basis continues
author: a changed basis restarts the count
author: returning to an earlier basis starts from 1
author: a first turn end continues
none: the first turn end continues with the directive
none: the second turn end on one basis ends the chain
none: the count carries across the actor, the K-th turn end on one basis ends

sequences.name: author, one basis: the reason, the notice that asks for action, the residual before the bound, the end
author, a basis that changes at every turn end: the same, by the T-th turn end of the chain
none: the directive is the residual from the first turn end, and the second on one basis ends
